restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) with its 37-step characteristic, two-bit conditions and the Step-1 solution S read off its published SFS pair as transcribed in filing 6c77089c, the 782,800 A0-variants of the 222 c7-classes with at least 3456 variants (1c368173, b947b377, 1f12a09a), and the packed row-16 stage of 7319bba. New: because x = A_{-1} takes only 2^32 values while about 2^58.3 first blocks are drawn, a table indexed by x (preprocessing, proof.md Section 8.2) stores for each passing class the partition of its variants into fibres of equal W6 value, the bit planes of the fibre values, and the member blocks; online one read at x and one bit-sliced 32-bit addition of cb = C6 - A_{-2} with the F6 test per 256 fibres (200 counted operations) replace the W7 and W6 programs. The set of good pairs is identical to the earlier filings' (Lemma 8.1).

Cost: fixed caps N_FB = 358,768,880,796,199,274 first blocks (2^58.31583; each one target compression plus 51 counted operations) and V_MAX = 5,987,153,443,586,154,090,544 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded), with A_C = 2^60 (characteristic and SFS-pair search), A_S = 2^50 (Step-1 SAT solve), DEV = 2^40 (development) and 2^58 operations of preprocessing (proof.md Section 8.2): 2^61.714723 target compressions on every run (proof.md Section 11), claimed 61.71473. Every target compression is charged one unit; every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison and branch is one primitive; there is no decision-DAG pricing.

Success probability at least 0.39 (0.3900000024) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-74.03, the registered floor of the one-sided 99 percent lower bound of the preregistered 32-replicate sequential Monte-Carlo study B of 7319bba, not re-run here), H3 (given one success, at most 2^-9.4 further successes expected in the same first block) and H7, by a per-first-block Bonferroni bound and independence across first blocks; Chebyshev bounds the work-cap overflow (cap slack 2^-6) below 2^-24.02. No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory is a reported metric only: at most 2^50 bytes, dominated by the x-indexed table (about 1.5 x 10^10 records of at most 73,024 bytes; typically 2^48.8 bytes in all). baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score. The class and fibre statistics of the table are Tungsten sample means (proof.md Section 13.3, premise H9), not an enumeration of all 2^32 values of x.

heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings; their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values; in particular x = A_{-1} is uniform on 2^32 and independent of cb = C6 - A_{-2}, which is uniform on 2^32. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = |F7|/2^32 and Pr[W6x in F6 | W7x in F7] = p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly (for every x, each fibre of a passing class passes F6 with probability p6 over cb), and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence g = 782,800 x p7 x p6 = 830.99 good pairs per first block in expectation, the expected counts of the ledger, and independence of distinct first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs and row-16 passes per first block; the expected operation count of the counted program; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by 7319bba with the attack's own filters on real first blocks in C (2^21 and 2^23 first blocks: passing classes 7,400,134 and 29,545,568 against 7,388,160 and 29,552,640 expected; good pairs ratio 1.0034 and 1.0011; row-16 pairs z = +0.88, +0.51; 0 failures of the exact checks), and by this filing's counted program on 160,000 real first blocks (passing classes per first block 3.5265 against 3.5229, good pairs 821.1 against 830.99, row-16 passes per good pair 2.403e-04 against 2.4268e-4; mean counted operations 16,028 +- 198 against the ledger's 16,482). These are at most 2^23 trials, not 2^58; the organizer experiment a0-online-r37 checks functional exactness only and is not evidence for H1.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on at most 2^23 first blocks. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed (variance-to-mean ratio about 23,000 for good pairs); only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used. The table is indexed by the 32-bit word x, so H1 is also used as an assumption about that single word.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 782,800 selected variants and the 32 elements of L* of Pr[rows 16..36 of both members follow every cell and every printed two-bit condition closing at rows >= 16 (corrected reading A15[29] = A17[29])] satisfies q3_model = 2^-74.03 <= q3 <= 2^-70, where 2^-74.03 is the registered floor of the one-sided 99 percent Student lower bound (2^-74.0225) of the mean of the preregistered 32-replicate sequential Monte-Carlo study B (NP = 8192) of 7319bba.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g 32 q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10). The good pairs and the later rows are those of 7319bba; this filing changes only how the good pairs are found (Lemma 8.1).
heuristics.extrapolation: Lemma 7.1: rows 16..22 have exactly the same probability for every variant; a variant enters rows >= 23 only through W8 in W23 and W24, so only the four W24 conditions can depend on it. The SMC (exact row 16, exact importance weights at rows 17..21, (W6, W7) uniform on F6 x F7, W8 drawn from the 782,800 variants) was preregistered twice by 7319bba (study A, NP = 2048: mean 2^-74.0187, bound 2^-74.0659; study B, NP = 8192, registered after study A had been read: mean 2^-73.9987, relative sd 0.038, bound 2^-74.0225). Stage factors 16.994, 13.000, 15.001, 6.000, 7.000, 1.000, 10.998 and 4.007 bits equal the per-row condition counts of the printed tables (74). 37-step semi-free-start collisions built with variants of the 222 classes verify under the repository verifier (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37: 127 of 128 local trials). The claim priced with study A's value is 61.74265.
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo bound produced by another solver and not re-run here (its programs are reproduced as inert text in proof.md Appendix A.7-A.9); its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 32 replicates; row-22 survivors are heavily duplicated within a replicate; study B was chosen after reading study A (disclosed and priced); depends on the reading of the '+' cells. No organizer experiment estimates q3; the organizer experiments verify only constructed semi-free-start witnesses. A stated premise, not an established fact.

heuristics.statement: For every trial t = (first block, variant, l), the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4. Equivalently: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10). The good pairs of a first block, and their dependence structure, are those of 7319bba (Lemma 8.1); the table changes only the order in which they are processed.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 7319bba's replay of 19,620,436 distinct Step-3 successes of the SMC: rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 14..36 gave 0 further successes (rule-of-three 95 percent bound 2^-22.65 per success; the samples share SMC ancestors). (b) With q3 <= 2^-70 (H2), the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x 782,800 x 32 x q3 <= rho x 2^-45.42, i.e. at most 2^-10.42 for rho <= 2^35; the measured factor at the row-16 level over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks is 0.98 and 1.00. Not re-measured here.
heuristics.limitations: Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly within one first block; the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor. The replay samples are correlated through SMC resampling. Participant-run measurements of another solver; no organizer experiment tests the late-round dependence. A stated premise, not an established fact.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice. Their construction is charged A_S = 2^50 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair) and A_C = 2^60 (the unpublished characteristic search); all development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the classes, the filter sets, L*, the row-16 table, the x-indexed table and the program text are recomputed in the preprocessing (2^58 operations bound).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^60.00155) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 11.3. A_S: 2^8.7 times the paper's reported Step-1 cost; the completion of a Step-1 solution to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about 25 milliseconds per pair (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37). A_C: at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted, promoted filing 6eeefb64 (2^21.427 units at C = 2644 per solver CPU-second), 2^60 units is 2^38.57 CPU-seconds, about 13,000 CPU-years: 688,000 times the 593,858 CPU-seconds that filing charged as a measured complete re-run of the predecessor 35-step characteristic search. The same allowances are charged by the accepted filings 087a18c4, 1f12a09a and 7319bba on this track.
heuristics.limitations: The 37-step characteristic search time is unpublished; A_C is a bound by comparison with the accepted measurement of the predecessor search, not a measurement of this one. A_C = 2^64 would give 64.19238 and A_C = 2^56 61.22949 (proof.md Section 11.2).

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a word-RAM program of 256-bit primitives in which every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison, branch and jump is one primitive is charged by the primitives it executes. The x-indexed table (T0 and the records R(x)) is ordinary memory built by a charged preprocessing; a read is an address computation plus one load; memory is a reported metric only. The fibre test of a batch of 256 fibres (adding the broadcast planes of cb to the 32 planes of fibre values and applying F6) is straight-line code of exactly 200 primitives (201 for a partial batch), independent of the data, with at most about 40 live registers of 64. The program text is not advice.
heuristics.scope: The fibre-test term (2,304 of the 16431.31 data-dependent operations per first block), the table reads (about 550 loads per first block) and the preprocessing bound (2^58 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The program is experiments/xtab.py (w6_batch asserts its count of 200; process_cv counts every operation of the online phase). It is exact against the scalar definitions: every lane of every pass plane equals the F6 test of its fibre value (9,556 lanes in the selftest and every lane of every processed class in a0-online-r37) and the member sets equal the brute-force good sets (5,882 good pairs, 0 mismatches). The counted program agrees with the ledger on 160,000 real first blocks (mean 16,028 +- 198 operations against 16,482).
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited. The premise that a table of up to 2^50 bytes is admissible follows the cost model's statement that memory contributes nothing to the scalar and earlier claims on this track with memory up to 2^137 bytes. A reader who charges memory or table reads differently should read proof.md Section 11.2: the table reads are about 3 percent of the data-dependent operations, and the preprocessing (2^58 operations, 2^46.6 units) is about 2^-15 of the score.

heuristics.statement: The cap target is mu0 = 0.49466252, the smallest 8-decimal number strictly above -ln(0.61 - Pcap - 2^-60) / (1 - 2^-10.4) with Pcap = 2^-24.02 the Chebyshev bound for the work cap. With E[X] >= mu0 the success bound of proof.md Section 10, 1 - exp(-(1 - 2^-10.4) mu0) - Pcap - 2^-60, is >= 0.39000000 with no further padding.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every allowance is an explicit term of the floor equation: the Chebyshev cap-failure bound Pcap (priced in proof.md Section 10 from the exact vmax_fb and vbar of the ledger), the repeated-first-block allowance 2^-60, and the H3 dependence discount as the divisor (1 - 2^-10.4). xtab.py computes mu0 with 60-digit decimals, iterates Pcap and N_FB to a fixed point, and asserts the success bound > 0.39. This is 087a18c4's H7.
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the equation makes the success arithmetic exact rather than adding slack.

heuristics.statement: (a) The means, over the x for which a class passes W7, of the number of fibres, of ceil(fibres/256) and of the number of 4-groups of the members (f_c, b_c, q_c of proof.md Section 12) are at most 1.02 times the mean of three independent Tungsten samples of 1,500 values of x per class (aggregate differences between the samples at most 0.31 percent, 0.26 percent and 0.05 percent). (b) The preprocessing of proof.md Section 8.2 costs at most 2^58 operations and the table at most 2^50 bytes.
heuristics.scope: The fibre-test, scan and member-block terms of the ledger (64 percent of the data-dependent operations) and the preprocessing and memory figures.
heuristics.extrapolation: Per-class means for all 222 classes are the constant STATS of xtab.py; per class the three samples differ by 2.6 percent on average (up to 10.5 percent for the fibre count), which averages out in the ledger sum over classes. Sensitivity (proof.md Section 11.2): all table statistics at face value 61.70388, 10 percent higher 61.75734, 50 percent higher 61.95335. The partition of every class into fibres was verified against brute force on every tested (class, x, cb) combination (selftest and a0-online-r37). Part (b) is an explicit algorithm with an explicit operation count (sort of at most 3600 records by the bottom-up merge sort bound of the organizer baseline, stated in proof.md Section 8.2).
heuristics.limitations: The means are sample estimates, not an enumeration over all 2^32 values of x. The memory (2^50 bytes) is far beyond physical machines; it is a reported metric only under collision-frontier-v5. The preprocessing is never executed in full by the organizer experiments, which build the records of single values of x on the fly.
